sections.content:
The only difference is the top HUD bar (row 0: W→w/g) — the board is identical to the pre-t15 state. That is, the board state is the same, the lock position is the same, yet the click does nothing now, but at t16 it worked.
What's different? The sequence of past actions? Maybe there's a "selection" state: at t15 I clicked (16,14) = cell c1 (a dot cell). That click did nothing to the dots, but maybe it "selected" something. Then at t16, clicking c3 merged c1+c2. Hmm, but which pair? c1+c2 merged into c3. If c1 had been selected... no, actually the merge rule might be this: clicking an empty cell adjacent to a dot moves the dot? No — two dots disappeared and one appeared.
Wait, let me reconsider: maybe the rule is "click an empty cell; the two adjacent dots (left and right, or the closest pair) merge into it." At t16, clicking c3: adjacent dots are c2 (left) and c4 (right) → they merge into c3?? But c4 remained, and c1+c2 disappeared. Before: c1, c2, c4, c6. After: c3, c4, c6. So c1+c2 → c3. c3's adjacent dots: only c2 (left) and c4 (right). c1 is not adjacent to c3. So the pair is c2+c4? But c4 remained... no, after: c3, c4, c6 — c4 is still there. So the pair that merged = c1+c2 (both to the left of c3?). c1 is at distance 2.
Another possibility: the pair = two dots in the same row, and clicking a cell between/adjacent to them merges them into the clicked cell. c1, c2 are adjacent to each other; c3 is adjacent to c2. So "click a cell adjacent to an adjacent pair" → the pair merges into the clicked cell.
t20: click c5 (37): before c3, c4, c6. Adjacent pair: c3+c4. c5 is adjacent to c4. → c3+c4 merge into c5. After: c5, c6. ✓.
t22: click c4 (31): before c5, c6. Pair c5+c6; c4 is adjacent to c5 → merge into c4. After: c4 (gray). ✓.
So the rule: click an empty cell adjacent to an adjacent dot pair → the pair merges into the clicked cell.
Now, why did the current m1 click (16,26)=c3 do nothing? Before: c1, c2, c4, c6 — the pair c1+c2 is adjacent, and c3 is adjacent to c2. It should have worked!
Maybe... the click coordinates: (16,26). Cell c3 spans columns 25-30? Cell width 6: c0=7-12? Wait, the cell columns are 7, 13, 19, 25, 31, 37, 43, and each cell is 4x4? The dot at column 13 has pixels 12 (a 3x3 with a hole?). The cell (white) has pixels 16 = 4x4. So cell c3 = columns 25-28, rows 15-18. (16,26) is inside. ✓ Same as t16.
So why doesn't it work now??
Difference: the state of the bottom board? At t16, the bottom dot was at (51,43) — same as now. The lock is at (33,31) — same.
Difference: maybe the game requires a "turn" — like, the board only accepts clicks on alternating turns? Or there's a cooldown after moving the lock?
Or: the click at t15 (16,14) was a "select" that enabled the merge! At t15, I clicked cell c1 (a dot cell). Maybe clicking a dot selects it (highlighted?), and then clicking an empty cell merges the selected dot with its neighbor?
t15: click c1 (dot) → select c1? (no visible change). t16: click c3 → merge c1+c2 into c3? Hmm, but that's not "selected + adjacent."
Or t15's click selected the pair...
Let me test directly: click the dot cell c1 (16,14), then click c3 (16,26), and check.
